description: Recorded LLM output for offline fallback. Incident summary for the Harbourfront One L23 chilled-water leak, as of 08:20.

summary.headline: Chilled-water leak at the AHU-23-01 supply branch above the L22 bank tenant ceiling; water reached DB-23A trunking; re-energisation of AHU-23-01 / DB-23A blocked pending LEW sign-off.
summary.location: L23 ceiling void / CHW riser R2 branch, above L22 tenant ceiling
summary.timeline_summary: At 08:02 leak detector LD-23-04 alarmed, followed by an AHU-23-01 chilled-water ΔT anomaly and a call from the bank facilities desk at 08:04. A P1 work order linked the isolation diagram. At 08:07 the technician found an active chilled-water leak at the AHU-23-01 supply branch; at 08:09 water was tracking toward distribution board DB-23A (about 1.5 m). The branch sub-valve ISV-L23-CHW was closed at 08:09:42 with the riser left open. At 08:11 AHU-23-01 was switched off and its DB-23A circuit isolated after water reached the control panel and trunking. The duty LEW was called at 08:12 (ETA 08:39). The bank reported wet ceiling tiles and workstations at 08:15; the next tenant update is set for 08:50.

key_decisions.text: Re-energising AHU-23-01 / DB-23A is blocked: LEW sign-off, insulation resistance test and area-dry confirmation are missing. Duty LEW Rahul Menon dispatched.
Water tracking toward the L23 electrical riser cupboard — nobody enters; escalated to the duty LEW.
Branch sub-valve ISV-L23-CHW closed at 08:09:42, 7 minutes after the alarm. Riser R2 left open.
First notice to the affected L22 tenant drafted; awaiting the Tenant Experience Manager's approval. 30-minute clock from the 08:04 call — due 08:34.
Anchor tenant: account manager Clare Tan to phone the bank's facilities director.

summary.current_risk: Flow stopped, but moisture at the DB-23A cupboard threshold is 18% against a 12% baseline. No water inside the cupboard. Re-energising before the LEW tests and signs off risks a short or arc flash.
